opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Jesus is preparing His disciples for what it will mean to follow Him. He isn’t promising them comfort—He’s preparing them for opposition.

“If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!”

What does it mean?

Beelzebul (or Beelzebub) was a name used for Satan, the “prince of demons.” Earlier in Matthew’s Gospel, the religious leaders accused Jesus of casting out demons by the power of Satan instead of by the power of God. It was one of the most insulting accusations they could make. Jesus is saying:

“If people falsely accused Me, the Master, of being evil, don’t be surprised if they falsely accuse you too.”

The “household” refers to His followers. If the Head of the household was slandered, the members should expect similar treatment.

Jesus is redefining what success looks like in the Christian life. Being misunderstood, criticized, or even rejected does not necessarily mean you’ve done something wrong. Sometimes it means you’re walking the same road He walked.
Following Christ doesn’t guarantee the approval of the world. It often invites misunderstanding because the values of God’s kingdom challenge the values of the world.

This verse can be unsettling, but it’s also deeply reassuring. Jesus doesn’t send His disciples into hardship blindly. He tells them beforehand:

“You won’t experience anything I haven’t already endured.”

There is comfort in knowing that when we are criticized for doing what is right, we are sharing—however imperfectly—in Christ’s own experience. We don’t seek persecution or conflict, but neither should we be shaken when faithfulness is misunderstood.

Whose approval matters most? If I live only for the approval of others, my faith will always be fragile. But if my desire is to please Christ, then criticism loses much of its power. The One who knows the truth about me is the One I ultimately answer to. “So do not be afraid of them.” (Matthew 10:26)

The message is clear: remain faithful. Christ has already walked this path, and He walks it with us still.
